title: Low-cost synthesis of peptide libraries for binding studies via intensity change
author: Schulte, Khayenko, et al.
materials: The here presented protocol encompasses standard SPPS using DIC and Oxyma for coupling, which exhibit higher stability over time than other coupling reagents such as COMU (El-Faham and Albericio, 2010) and are easier to handle than HOBT (Subirós-Funosas et al., 2009). Due to inadequate half-life for automated synthesis, we recommend to employ acetic anhydride for capping without an additional, sterically hindered base (Pon et al., 1999) but longer incubation steps and repetition.22.Prepare stock solutions of the aa building blocks at a concentration of 0.5 M in DMF.Note: Certain aas, especially Fmoc-Pro-OH and Fmoc-Phe-OH, might need extra agitation to fully dissolve. We recommend dissolving these derivates on an orbital shaker for 1 h at ambient conditions.23.Prepare solutions of DIC and OxymaPure at a concentration of 1 M in DMF and acetic anhydride (Ac2O) at 4% (v/v) in DMFNote: Since these solutions need to be exchanged every 48–72 h, we recommend preparing 15 mL of DIC and Oxyma stock solutions and 30 mL of Ac2O stock solution each time in a 50 mL falcon tube.24.Prepare 180 mL of a deprotection solution containing 20% (v/v) pip in DMFa.Commonly, more than 180 mL (the max volume of reagent containers in a MultiPep 2 synthesizer) are needed for one synthesis. Therefore, it is advised to pay attention to the amount of deprotection solution left in the container during synthesis and refill it accordingly.Note: We recommend preparing the aa stock solutions in advance. The reagents however should be prepared on the same day as the synthesis is started.Pause point: Stock solutions of aa derivates in DMF can be stored at −80°C for several months.

Timing: 30 min40.In Di.Control, a dilution series ID is assigned to each well of a measured dataset. That way wells are grouped as one single dilution series for further analysis.41.On the ligands page in DI.ScreeningAnalysis, select the “use merge sets” function that merges replicates of dilution series of the same ligand, depending on the ligand name. Dilution series are then shown as merged data sets that are approximated by a global fit to all datapoints (Figure 7A).Figure 7DI.ScreeningAnalysis dose-response(A) In the “ligands” section, the “merge sets” feature can be used to merge replicate datasets for analysis. Furthermore, the “use hill-fit” feature should be applied accordingly to the experimental setup. Additionally, individual datapoints may be manually inspected.(B) In the “summary” section, overviews are automatically generated, and analyzed datasets may be exported.42.Depending on the assay conditions, select or deselect “use Hill fit” (Figure 7A).Note: The Hill fit is only recommended for competition assays or assays with known cooperativity. For direct binding of one ligand to one target molecule, the function is deselected and a law of mass action-based KD fitting algorithm is commonly used.43.We recommend manual inspection of all ligands for smaller datasets to review software decisions, such as aggregation or ligand-induced quenching (Figure 7A).44.Use the batch export on the summary page of DI.ScreeningAnalysis to export vector graphics of dose-response plots and raw-data values and fit parameters in a tabular format for further use (Figure 7B).

steps.title: Prepare functionalized cellulose disks
steps.instruction: Cut, dry, functionalize, wash and dry cellulose sheets to generate solid support for peptide synthesis.

substeps.instruction: Cut Whatman paper sheets into 15 × 10 cm pieces using a paper trimmer.
Dry the cut sheets under vacuum in a desiccator for at least 8 h; optionally wrap each sheet in a Kimtech‑wipe envelope for easier handling.

Prepare functionalization mix for 6 sheets: dissolve 3.7 g Fmoc‑β‑Ala‑OH in 50 mL DMF, add 2.3 mL DIC and 0.96 mL 1‑Methylimidazole (NMI), then bring the total volume to 60 mL DMF. Final concentrations are 0.2 M Fmoc‑β‑Ala‑OH (1 eq), 0.24 M DIC (1.2 eq) and 0.2 M NMI (1 eq).

In a fume hood, place each sheet in a flat plastic container (Raaco, part no.: 136129) with 10 mL of the functionalization mix; incubate on an orbital shaker at ~60 rpm for 3 h, flipping the sheets after 1.5 h with a metal tweezer.
Discard the mix and wash each sheet sequentially with 3 × 10 mL DMF (1 min each) followed by 3 × 10 mL EtOH (1 min each), holding the sheet with a metal tweezer during each wash.
Allow the EtOH to evaporate for ~15 min in the fume hood.
Finish drying the sheets in a desiccator for at least another 8 h.

steps.title: Prepare amino‑acid derivatives and reagents
steps.instruction: Make all stock solutions required for SPPS and store them appropriately.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.5 M amino‑acid (aa) stock solutions in DMF; for Fmoc‑Pro‑OH and Fmoc‑Phe‑OH, place the vials on an orbital shaker for 1 h at ambient temperature to ensure complete dissolution.

Prepare 1 M DIC stock and 1 M OxymaPure stock in DMF (15 mL each) and a 4 % (v/v) acetic anhydride (Ac₂O) solution in DMF (30 mL). Use 50 mL Falcon tubes for each preparation; refresh these solutions every 48–72 h.

Prepare 180 mL deprotection solution containing 20 % (v/v) piperidine (pip) in DMF. Note that a MultiPep 2 reagent container holds a maximum of 180 mL, so monitor the volume during synthesis and refill as needed.
Store aa‑DMF stock solutions at –80 °C for several months; prepare DIC, OxymaPure and Ac₂O stocks on the same day synthesis is started.

steps.title: Set up MultiPep 2 synthesizer
steps.instruction: Load sequences, reagents, disks and configure the robot before running the synthesis.

substeps.instruction: Enter peptide sequences in the MultiPep 2‑CelluSpots software and save them as a .SEQ file.

Generate a report sheet (Show Report → Refill=Used) to calculate the required volume of each building block; add the “mL actual” volume (including dead volume) to the corresponding 10 mL reaction tubes.

Place the 10 mL reaction tubes (containing aa, DIC, Oxyma, Ac₂O) and the 2 mL mixer tubes into the designated positions of the reagent rack (re‑use cleaned 10 mL tubes; discard mixer tubes after synthesis).
Empty the waste container connected to the vacuum pump and verify an airtight connection by briefly running the pump.
Connect the 384‑format rack to the vacuum pump, ensuring a tight seal (see Fig. 3).

Transfer the functionalized cellulose disks onto 384‑well trays, verify that each disk sits securely in its well, close the rack, and if only one tray is used, place an empty second tray sealed with a 384‑well silicon mat to maintain vacuum.
Fill the washing reservoirs with DMF and EtOH, and place the Pip, DIC, Oxyma and Ac₂O reservoirs in the positions indicated by the report sheet.
Manually move the robot needle to a corner well of each 384‑well plate (Go‑to command) and adjust X, Y, Z coordinates as needed (increase X → right, increase Y → forward, increase Z → down).
Prime the syringe with DMF and EtOH in the Manual section of the software, removing all air bubbles from the tubing.

steps.title: Single‑dose screening data analysis
steps.instruction: Process raw TRIC measurements to identify hit ligands.

substeps.instruction: In DI.Control, assign a reference ID to each well (reference = target‑only). Place references in duplicate rows according to the 4‑channel STARlet pipetting layout.
Load all relevant files into DI.ScreeningAnalysis and select the experiments to analyse.
On the Data page, set the hit‑threshold multiplier (z‑score factor) to 7 (default is 3‑fold global SD).
Manually inspect all reference wells for aggregation bias and exclude problematic references.
Inspect the ligand page; manually re‑categorise ligands if the automatic algorithm mis‑labels hits, non‑binders, or aggregators.
Export the curated ligand list and associated categories from the Summary page for downstream dose‑response experiments.

steps.title: Dose‑response data analysis
steps.instruction: Fit dilution‑series data to obtain affinity parameters.

substeps.instruction: In DI.Control, assign a dilution‑series ID to each well of the dataset.
In DI.ScreeningAnalysis, use the “use merge sets” function on the Ligands page to merge replicates of the same ligand’s dilution series.
Select or deselect “use Hill fit” depending on assay type (Hill fit for competition/cooperativity assays; deselect for 1:1 binding where a mass‑action KD fit is used).
Manually review merged datasets for artifacts such as aggregation or ligand‑induced quenching.
Export dose‑response plots (vector graphics) and raw data with fit parameters from the Summary page.

steps.title: Interpret ligand categories
steps.instruction: Classify ligands according to the categories defined in Table 3 for single‑dose and dose‑response TRIC measurements.

description: Here, we provide a cost-effective approach for high-throughput studies of protein-peptide interactions, specifically with temperature-related intensity change (TRIC) measurements using the Dianthus NT.23 system (Nanotemper Technologies GmbH). Using state of the art peptide chemistry and the currently available materials, we also provide an updated version of the popular cellulose-based SC2 (Dikmans et al., 2006, McBride et al., 2016) and SPOT (Frank, 1992, Mao et al., 2021) approaches. The protocol is tailored for the automated and parallel peptide synthesis with the MultiPep 2 (CEM GmbH) or similar liquid handling systems and scaled towards the need of the high-throughput affinity determination in solution. Laser cutting to minimize hands-on time and cost of solid support preparation and quality control using mass spectrometry are highly recommended but optional. The protocol combines synthesis and evaluation, maintaining the cost-effectiveness of the widely available cellulose-based peptide synthesis approaches and their seamless transition into in-solution TRIC measurements.
